claim: At least 25 different, transmembrane domain (TMD)-containing E3s are predicted to be ER-localised.
source: At least 25 different, transmembrane domain (TMD)-containing E3s are predicted to be ER-localised, but for most their organisation and cellular roles remain poorly defined.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a prediction based on analysis.

claim: A comparative proteomic workflow mapped over 450 protein-protein interactions for 21 stably expressed, full-length E3s.
source: Using a comparative proteomic workflow, we mapped over 450 protein-protein interactions for 21 stably expressed, full-length E3s.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results from the study.

claim: RNF26 is a polytopic E3 whose abundance is auto-regulated by ubiquitin-proteasome dependent degradation.
source: Among these were four membrane-embedded interactors of RNF26, a polytopic E3 whose abundance is auto-regulated by ubiquitin-proteasome dependent degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: RNF26 co-assembles with TMEM43, ENDOD1, TMEM33 and TMED1 to form a complex.
source: RNF26 co-assembles with TMEM43, ENDOD1, TMEM33 and TMED1 to form a complex capable of modulating innate immune signalling through the cGAS-STING pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by co-immunoprecipitation and velocity sedimentation data in Figure 5.

claim: The RNF26 complex is capable of modulating innate immune signalling through the cGAS-STING pathway.
source: RNF26 co-assembles with TMEM43, ENDOD1, TMEM33 and TMED1 to form a complex capable of modulating innate immune signalling through the cGAS-STING pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by functional data in Figure 6 showing effects on IFIT1 transcription.

claim: The RNF26 complex represents a new modulatory axis of STING and innate immune signalling at the ER membrane.
source: This RNF26 complex represents a new modulatory axis of STING and innate immune signalling at the ER membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: The ER can occupy more than 35% of the entire cell volume.
source: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is the largest membrane-bound organelle in eukaryotic cells, comprised of a complex network of sheets, tubules, junctions and contact sites that can occupy more than 35% of the entire cell volume (Valm et al., 2017) and a significant fraction of the total membrane surface area.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Valm et al., 2017.

claim: The ER forms a continuous lattice with the nuclear envelope.
source: The continuous lattice it forms with the nuclear envelope (NE) makes extensive and dynamic contacts through distal projections with mitochondria (Kornmann et al., 2009), peroxisomes (Smith and Aitchison, 2013), endosomes (van der Kant and Neefjes, 2014; Hönscher and Ungermann, 2014), plasma membrane (Saheki and De Camilli, 2017) and lipid droplets (reviewed in Wu et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The ER makes extensive and dynamic contacts with mitochondria.
source: The continuous lattice it forms with the nuclear envelope (NE) makes extensive and dynamic contacts through distal projections with mitochondria (Kornmann et al., 2009), peroxisomes (Smith and Aitchison, 2013), endosomes (van der Kant and Neefjes, 2014; Hönscher and Ungermann, 2014), plasma membrane (Saheki and De Camilli, 2017) and lipid droplets (reviewed in Wu et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Kornmann et al., 2009.

claim: There are more than 600 Ub ligases (E3s) in the mammalian cell.
source: The enzymatic cascade conjugating and extending Ub chains on proteins throughout the mammalian cell uses one (or more) of the >600 Ub ligases (E3s) to provide reaction specificity by bringing substrates and Ub conjugating enzymes (E2s) in proximity (Li et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Li et al., 2008.

claim: About 10% of E3s contain TMDs that tether affiliated processes to lipid bilayers.
source: Of the >600 E3s present in the human proteome, about 10% contain TMDs that tether affiliated processes to lipid bilayers.
evidence: This is stated as a calculation based on the total number of E3s and those with TMDs.

claim: More than 80% of ER-E3s tested (21/25) could be detected from whole cell lysates.
source: More than 80% of ER-E3s tested (21/25) could be detected from whole cell lysates (WCL), accumulating in a DOX-dependent manner that reflects relative stability (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Including MG132 along with DOX enhanced detection of some E3s (e.g. RNF26, BFAR, TMEM129).
source: Including MG132 along with DOX enhanced detection of some E3s (e.g. RNF26, BFAR, TMEM129), indicative of intrinsic instability and constitutive turnover by proteasome-mediated degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: E3s co-localised exclusively (or partly) with the ER-markers calnexin or KDEL.
source: E3s co-localised exclusively (or partly) with the ER-markers calnexin or KDEL (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), consistent with their expected residency in the ER.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cofactors including SEL1L, FAM8A1, OS-9, Herp, and UBE2J1 were comparably co-immunoprecipitated by both Hrd1 and Hrd1-FH.
source: Cofactors including SEL1L, FAM8A1, OS-9, Herp, and UBE2J1 were comparably co-immunoprecipitated (co-IPed) by both Hrd1 and Hrd1-FH (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 1C.

claim: Hrd1-FH complexes migrate in fractions that overlap with those formed by endogenous Hrd1.
source: Moreover, velocity sedimentation revealed that Hrd1-FH complexes migrate in fractions that overlap with those formed by endogenous Hrd1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by velocity sedimentation data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Approximately 1600 individual protein groups were detected within each sample.
source: Approximately 1600 individual protein groups were detected within each sample.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the mass spectrometry results.

claim: In total, >2000 unique proteins were identified.
source: In total, >2000 unique proteins were identified (Supplementary file 1, Table 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the mass spectrometry results.

claim: 218 different HCIPs that formed 403 interactions were identified from the 21 E3 ligases examined.
source: From the 21 E3 ligases we comparatively examined, 218 different HCIPs that formed 403 interactions were identified (Supplementary file 1, Table 5).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results.

claim: Over 50% of HCIPs (111/218) were significantly enriched by just one ER-E3.
source: Importantly, over 50% of HCIPs (111/218) were significantly enriched by just one ER-E3 while those remaining associated with 2 (66/218), 3 (20/218) or >4 (21/218) different ligases (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the distribution shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Approximately two-thirds of HCIPs (139/218) contained features consistent with localisation to the endomembrane system.
source: Approximately two-thirds of HCIPs (139/218) contained features consistent with localisation to the endomembrane system, validating our enrichment strategy for ER-associated proteins (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the classification shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Only ~13% of E3-HCIP interactions were reported previously in BioGRID 3.5 and BioPlex 3.0.
source: The originality of the E3 interactions identified is reflected by their underrepresentation in current protein-protein interaction resources (BioGRID 3.5 and BioPlex 3.0), where only ~13% of E3-HCIP interactions were reported previously (Oughtred et al., 2019; Huttlin et al., 2020; Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations and supported by Figure 2G.

claim: CGRRF1, RNF13, RNF170 and RNFT1 transcript levels increased with acute ER stress (~2 fold).
source: CGRRF1, RNF13, RNF170 and RNFT1 transcript levels increased with acute ER stress (~2 fold) as reported previously (Kaneko et al., 2016), along with RNF5 (Tm only) and RNF139 (SubAB only) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and supported by NanoString data in Figure 3B.

claim: siRNA-mediated knockdowns of endogenous isoforms were not sufficient to induce the splicing of XBP1.
source: Moreover, ER homeostatic maintenance did not require any individual ER-E3 since siRNA-mediated knockdowns of endogenous isoforms were not sufficient to induce the splicing of XBP1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), consistent with CRISPRi screens for ER stress induction (Adamson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and supported by XBP1 splicing assay data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: VCP/p97 enrichment was among the highest for gp78/AMFR and Hrd1.
source: Among the highest were those for gp78/AMFR and Hrd1, in line with their established recruitment for ERAD, but RNF185, MARCH4 and RNF5 were also within the upper quartile (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by spectral count data in Figure 3C.

claim: RNF185, MARCH4 and RNF5 were within the upper quartile for VCP/p97 enrichment.
source: Among the highest were those for gp78/AMFR and Hrd1, in line with their established recruitment for ERAD, but RNF185, MARCH4 and RNF5 were also within the upper quartile (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by spectral count data in Figure 3C.

claim: The soluble VCP/p97 cofactors UFD1 and NPLOC4 were HCIPs of RNF185.
source: The soluble VCP/p97 cofactors UFD1 and NPLOC4 were also HCIPs of RNF185 (Figure 3A, and discussed below), which lends additional support for this E3 in an ERAD-related role (El Khouri et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and supported by the heat map in Figure 3A.

claim: RNF185 was highlighted among the set of prominent candidates identified in the VCP/p97 interactome.
source: RNF185 was recently highlighted among the set of prominent candidates identified in the VCP/p97 interactome (Hülsmann et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Hülsmann et al., 2018.

claim: RNF170 and RNF185 enriched for the ERLIN1/2 heterodimer.
source: We identified enrichment of the ERLIN1/2 heterodimer by RNF170 and RNF185, and ERLIN1 alone by RNF5 and gp78/AMFR (Figures 2C and 3A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 2C and 3A.

claim: IP3R was only enriched by RNF170.
source: IP3R was only enriched by RNF170, in line with its previous identification as a cognate substrate and demonstrating that this methodology can also identify bona fide E3 substrates.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the proteomic data.

claim: 23 different HCIPs were involved in the biosynthesis and regulation of cholesterol, fatty acids, or phospholipids.
source: 23 different HCIPs were involved in the biosynthesis and regulation of cholesterol, fatty acids, or phospholipids, with 80% annotated as TMD-containing proteins residing in the ER (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the heat map in Figure 3D.

claim: HMGCR was among the HCIPs of gp78/AMFR.
source: Among the HCIPs of gp78/AMFR was HMGCR, previously reported as its substrate (Jo et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to Jo et al., 2011a.

claim: Endogenous RNF26 protein could not be detected from whole cell lysates.
source: Despite efforts and consistent with published data (Jongsma et al., 2016), endogenous RNF26 protein could not be detected from whole cell lysates, even though relative mRNA levels in HEK293 cells were comparable to other E3s such as Hrd1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and supported by transcript data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Stabilisation by MG132 reflected intrinsic instability of RNF26 and suggested constitutive disposal by ERAD or an ERAD-like process.
source: Stabilisation by MG132 reflected intrinsic instability of RNF26 and suggested constitutive disposal by ERAD or an ERAD-like process.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the MG132 stabilization data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: A neutralising mutation (Y432A) stabilises FH-RNF26 protein levels and renders it insensitive to MG132.
source: This aromatic residue is conserved in RNF26 (Y432, Figure 4A and B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), where a neutralising mutation (Y432A) stabilises FH-RNF26 protein levels and renders it insensitive to MG132 (Figure 4C, middle panel).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 4C.

claim: Radiolabel pulse-chase assays confirmed the increased stability of newly synthesised FH-RNF26Y432A compared to FH-RNF26WT (t1/2 ~ 2 hrs. vs. <0.5 hr).
source: Radiolabel pulse-chase assays confirmed the increased stability of newly synthesised FH-RNF26Y432A compared to FH-RNF26WT (t1/2 ~ 2 hrs. vs. <0.5 hr, Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by pulse-chase data in Figure 4D.

claim: Expression of FH-RNF26Y432A enabled endogenous RNF26 to be co-precipitated and detected.
source: Expression of FH-RNF26Y432A also enabled endogenous RNF26 to be co-precipitated and detected (Figure 4E), consistent with the formation of stable and inactive heterodimers.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 4E.

claim: Immunoprecipitated FH-RNF26WT produced FLAG-immunoreactive ladders and high-molecular weight smears, enhanced by MG132 and collapsed by the non-selective DUB Usp21.
source: Accordingly, immunoprecipitated FH-RNF26WT produced FLAG-immunoreactive ladders and high-molecular weight smears, enhanced by MG132 and collapsed by the non-selective DUB Usp21 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by TUBE pulldown data in Figure 4F.

claim: Immunoprecipitated FH-RNF26WT subjected to a panel of linkage specific DUBs indicated RNF26 modification by K33-, K63- and K29-linkages as well as multiple mono-ubiquitination.
source: Curiously however, immunoprecipitated FH-RNF26WT subjected to a panel of linkage specific DUBs indicated RNF26 modification by Ub chains not conventionally linked with degradation, including K33-, K63- and K29-linkages as well as multiple mono-ubiquitination (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by UbiCREST data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The inclusion of FH-RNF26Y432A increased the total number of high-confidence protein-protein interactions from 431 to 460.
source: The inclusion of FH-RNF26Y432A increased the total number of high-confidence protein-protein interactions from 431 to 460.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results.

claim: Prominent HCIPs of both RNF26 forms included TMEM43/LUMA and ENDOD1.
source: Prominent HCIPs of both RNF26 forms included TMEM43/LUMA (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), an evolutionarily ancient multi-spanning membrane protein present in both the ER and INM (Bengtsson and Otto, 2008; Dreger et al., 2001), and ENDOD1 (endonuclease domain containing-1), an uncharacterised polytopic protein containing a putative DNA/RNA non-specific nuclease domain (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations and supported by data in Figure 5B.

claim: RNF26Y432A enriched for TMED1, TMEM33, UBXD8 and AUP1.
source: RNF26Y432A also enriched for TMED1, an atypical member of the p24 cargo receptor family (Jenne et al., 2002), an ER membrane-shaping factor TMEM33 (Urade et al., 2014), as well as the ERAD and lipid droplet-related proteins UBXD8 and AUP1 (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations and supported by data in Figure 5A and B.

claim: FH-RNF26 was reproducibly brought down by S-tagged TMEM43, TMED1, AUP1 and UBXD8.
source: FH-RNF26 was reproducibly brought down by S-tagged TMEM43, TMED1, AUP1 and UBXD8, with the latter exhibiting a high molecular weight smear of RNF26 reminiscent of polyubiquitinated forms (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-precipitation data in Figure 5C.

claim: S-tagged TMEM43 and TMED1 were able to bring down endogenous ENDOD1 and TMEM33 (TMED1 only).
source: For reasons that are not clear, exogenous expression of S-tagged ENDOD1 and TMEM33 proved difficult to detect, however S-tagged TMEM43 and TMED1 were able to bring down endogenous ENDOD1 and TMEM33 (TMED1 only), indicating that these HCIPs comprised larger macromolecular complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-precipitation data in Figure 5C.

claim: Velocity sedimentation revealed a profile of a complex migrating between ~200–300 kDa (fractions 4–6) with endogenous TMEM43, TMED1, ENDOD1, TMEM33, UBXD8 and AUP1 co-sedimenting with FH-RNF26.
source: Velocity sedimentation of lysates from FH-RNF26WT expressing cells revealed a profile of a complex migrating between ~200–300 kDa (fractions 4–6) with endogenous TMEM43, TMED1, ENDOD1, TMEM33, UBXD8 and AUP1 co-sedimenting with FH-RNF26, albeit with varying degrees of overlap within fractions (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by velocity sedimentation data in Figure 5D.

claim: TMEM43 co-precipitated by FH-RNF26Y432A was independent of detergent conditions.
source: TMEM43 co-precipitated by FH-RNF26Y432A was independent of detergent conditions while other HCIP interactions were compromised to varying degrees in TX-100.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-precipitation data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Silencing TMEM43 disrupted the ability of FH-RNF26WT to co-precipitate other HCIPs.
source: Silencing TMEM43 disrupted the ability of FH-RNF26WT to co-precipitate other HCIPs, without substantially altering total cellular levels (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 5E.

claim: A reduction in immunoprecipitated RNF26 (both unmodified and ubiquitinated) resulted from ENDOD1 knockdown.
source: A reduction in immunoprecipitated RNF26 (both unmodified and ubiquitinated) resulted from ENDOD1 knockdown, which might underlie the lower levels of other HCIPs in RNF26 pulldowns, in particular TMED1.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 5E.

claim: Detection of both unmodified and ubiquitinated forms of RNF26 was markedly enhanced with the loss of TMED1.
source: Although the pattern of HCIPs co-precipitated by RNF26 was unaffected by depletion of either TMEM33 or TMED1, detection of both unmodified and ubiquitinated forms of RNF26 was markedly enhanced with the loss of TMED1.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 5E.

claim: siRNA-mediated depletion of TMEM43, TMEM33 or ENDOD1 did not markedly stabilise RNF26.
source: In cycloheximide (CHX) chase assays, siRNA-mediated depletion of TMEM43, TMEM33 or ENDOD1 did not markedly stabilise RNF26 nor did they alter turnover of immature CD147 (Figure 5F), a well-characterised Hrd1-dependent ERAD substrate (Tyler et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and supported by CHX chase data in Figure 5F.

claim: TMED1 knockdown resulted in a modest slowing of RNF26 degradation leading to an increase in overall RNF26 levels.
source: TMED1 knockdown resulted in a modest slowing of RNF26 degradation leading to an increase in overall RNF26 levels (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5E.

claim: VCP/p97 inhibition by NMS-873 only partially restored RNF26 while stabilising CD147 equivalently to MG132.
source: Of note, VCP/p97 inhibition by NMS-873 only partially restored RNF26 while stabilising CD147 equivalently to MG132 (Figures 5F and 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CHX chase data in Figure 5F.

claim: RNF26 was not among those E3s that enriched VCP/p97.
source: RNF26 was not among those E3s that enriched VCP/p97 (Figure 3C), potentially distinguishing its mechanism of turnover from that of a canonical, misfolded ERAD substrate.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by spectral count data in Figure 3C.

claim: RNF26 knockdown reduced STING protein levels by ~30%.
source: We observed that like RNF26 knockdown, TMED1 siRNAs reduced STING protein levels by ~30% whereas those targeting TMEM43, ENDOD1 or TMEM33 had little to no impact (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 6B and C.

claim: TMED1 siRNAs reduced STING protein levels by ~30%.
source: We observed that like RNF26 knockdown, TMED1 siRNAs reduced STING protein levels by ~30% whereas those targeting TMEM43, ENDOD1 or TMEM33 had little to no impact (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 6B and C.

claim: STING activation by cGAMP increased IFIT1 transcription ~3–4 fold in WT cells.
source: STING activation by cGAMP increased IFIT1 transcription ~3–4 fold in WT cells (Figure 6D and E) and did so in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 6D and E.

claim: RNF26 knockdown attenuated the increase in IFIT1.
source: RNF26 knockdown (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B) attenuated the increase in IFIT1, consistent with previous findings (Qin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 6D.

claim: Expression of FH-RNF26Y432A inhibited IFIT1 upregulation.
source: Expression of FH-RNF26Y432A also inhibited IFIT1 upregulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), demonstrating that the IFIT1 response requires ubiquitination by RNF26 and that the Y432A mutant functions as a dominant negative.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Knockdown of either TMED1 or ENDOD1 dampened the cGAMP-induced IFIT1 response.
source: Knockdown of either TMED1 or ENDOD1 also dampened the cGAMP-induced IFIT1 response (Figure 6D), but lower STING levels only coincided with TMED1 loss and not ENDOD1 (Figure 6B and C), suggesting these two HCIPs impact STING and signalling through it, by different mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 6D and western blot data in Figure 6B and C.

claim: Depleting cells of either TMEM43 or TMEM33 enhanced IFIT1 responses to cGAMP, resulting in 5–7-fold increases that were nearly twice the magnitude elicited from CTRL cells.
source: In marked contrast, depleting cells of either TMEM43 or TMEM33 enhanced IFIT1 responses to cGAMP, resulting in 5–7-fold increases that were nearly twice the magnitude elicited from CTRL cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 6D.

claim: Co-depleting RNF26 along with TMED1 or ENDOD1 did not attenuate IFIT1 responses further.
source: Co-depleting RNF26 along with TMED1 or ENDOD1 did not attenuate IFIT1 responses further, and co-depleting with either TMEM43 or TMEM33 reduced the enhanced IFIT1 responses by ~50% (Figure 6E), indicating that the impact of these HCIPs on STING activation was at least in part through RNF26.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 6E.

claim: Co-depleting RNF26 with either TMEM43 or TMEM33 reduced the enhanced IFIT1 responses by ~50%.
source: Co-depleting RNF26 along with TMED1 or ENDOD1 did not attenuate IFIT1 responses further, and co-depleting with either TMEM43 or TMEM33 reduced the enhanced IFIT1 responses by ~50% (Figure 6E), indicating that the impact of these HCIPs on STING activation was at least in part through RNF26.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 6E.

claim: Hrd1 was the only E3 upregulated by direct activation of either the XBP1 or ATF6 transcription factors.
source: This is consistent with the observation that Hrd1 was the only E3 upregulated by direct activation of either the XBP1 or ATF6 transcription factors (Shoulders et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Shoulders et al., 2013.

claim: There were only 24 HCIPs among known UPR target genes.
source: Moreover, there were only 24 HCIPs among known UPR target genes (Bergmann et al., 2018) with at least a quarter belonging to the Hrd1 complex (Supplementary file 1, Table 7, Christianson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Bergmann et al., 2018 and Christianson et al., 2012.

claim: Ubiquitination by the Hrd1 complex is essential for survival under proteotoxic ER stress conditions.
source: Thus, evolutionary expansion of E3s in the mammalian ER has not extensively supplemented adaptive stress-resolving capabilities functionally redundant with Hrd1, consistent with ubiquitination by the Hrd1 complex being essential for survival under proteotoxic ER stress conditions (Yagishita et al., 2005; Vitale et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Yagishita et al., 2005 and Vitale et al., 2019.

claim: RNF26 reportedly modifies STING with K11 chains.
source: For example, RNF26 reportedly modifies STING with K11 chains (Qin et al., 2014) but we showed its own turnover from the ER is rapid and is associated with K33-, K63- and/or K29-linked ubiquitin chains not conventionally associated with degradation or targeting to proteasomes.
evidence: This is stated with citation to Qin et al., 2014.

claim: RNF26's own turnover from the ER is rapid and is associated with K33-, K63- and/or K29-linked ubiquitin chains.
source: For example, RNF26 reportedly modifies STING with K11 chains (Qin et al., 2014) but we showed its own turnover from the ER is rapid and is associated with K33-, K63- and/or K29-linked ubiquitin chains not conventionally associated with degradation or targeting to proteasomes.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by UbiCREST data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: There are ~40 E2s and nearly ~100 DUBs in the human proteome.
source: As there are ~40 E2s and nearly ~100 DUBs in the human proteome, we would expect one (or more) to partner with each E3 to expand its substrate range.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the ubiquitin system.

claim: Functional roles in ERAD were identified for USP13, Atx3, VCPIP and USP19.
source: Similarly, functional roles in ERAD were identified for USP13, Atx3, VCPIP and USP19, but ER-E3s were not identified among the DUB interactome (Sowa et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Sowa et al., 2009.

claim: TMEM43 is the human orthologue of S. pombe Tts1.
source: TMEM33 is the human orthologue of S. pombe Tts1, an ER-shaping protein that helps sustain high-curvature ER membranes (Zhang et al., 2010) and is involved in nuclear envelope remodelling during mitosis (Zhang and Oliferenko, 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Zhang et al., 2010 and Zhang and Oliferenko, 2014.

claim: TMEM33 is an ER-shaping protein that helps sustain high-curvature ER membranes.
source: TMEM33 is the human orthologue of S. pombe Tts1, an ER-shaping protein that helps sustain high-curvature ER membranes (Zhang et al., 2010) and is involved in nuclear envelope remodelling during mitosis (Zhang and Oliferenko, 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Zhang et al., 2010.

claim: TMEM33 is involved in nuclear envelope remodelling during mitosis.
source: TMEM33 is the human orthologue of S. pombe Tts1, an ER-shaping protein that helps sustain high-curvature ER membranes (Zhang et al., 2010) and is involved in nuclear envelope remodelling during mitosis (Zhang and Oliferenko, 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Zhang and Oliferenko, 2014.

claim: TMEM43/LUMA localises in both the INM and the ER.
source: TMEM43/LUMA localises in both the INM and the ER and interacts with proteins such as Lamin A/B and Emerin (Bengtsson and Otto, 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Bengtsson and Otto, 2008.

claim: Mutations in TMEM43 are genetically linked to autosomal dominant arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy/dysplasia (ARVC/D, S358L).
source: Mutations in TMEM43 are genetically linked to the heritable cardiomyopathy autosomal dominant arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy/dysplasia (ARVC/D, S358L) (Merner et al., 2008) and the autosomal recessive myopathy Emery-Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy (EDMD, Q85K, I91V, [Liang et al., 2011]).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Merner et al., 2008.

claim: Mutations in TMEM43 are genetically linked to Emery-Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy (EDMD, Q85K, I91V).
source: Mutations in TMEM43 are genetically linked to the heritable cardiomyopathy autosomal dominant arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy/dysplasia (ARVC/D, S358L) (Merner et al., 2008) and the autosomal recessive myopathy Emery-Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy (EDMD, Q85K, I91V, [Liang et al., 2011]).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Liang et al., 2011.

claim: TMEM43 has been linked previously to immune signalling and NF-kB through an interaction with CARMA3/CARD10 and EGFR.
source: TMEM43 has been linked previously to immune signalling and NF-kB through an interaction with CARMA3/CARD10 and EGFR (Jiang et al., 2017), but not previously to STING.
evidence: This is stated with citation to Jiang et al., 2017.

claim: ENDOD1 is predicted to contain a non-specific endonuclease domain shown to have nuclease activity in vitro using an orthologous domain from Paralichthys olivaceus (Japanese flounder).
source: ENDOD1 is predicted to contain a non-specific endonuclease domain shown to have nuclease activity in vitro using an orthologous domain from Paralichthys olivaceus (Japanese flounder) (Lyu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Lyu et al., 2016.

claim: ENDOD1 was identified among the genes that are important for innate immunity in fish.

claim: The depletion of TOLLIP, an endocytic adaptor recruited by RNF26 to maintain endosomal positioning, results in the loss of steady-state STING levels.
source: This is supported by recent findings showing the depletion of TOLLIP, an endocytic adaptor recruited by RNF26 to maintain endosomal positioning (Jongsma et al., 2016), also results in the loss of steady-state STING levels (Pokatayev et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Jongsma et al., 2016 and Pokatayev et al., 2020.
